<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
               <jats:p>In this work we investigate how to quantify the coherence of quantum measurements. First, we establish a resource theoretical framework to address the coherence of measurement and show that any statistical distance can be adopted to define a coherence monotone of measurement. For instance, the relative entropy fulfills all the required properties as a proper monotone. We specifically introduce a coherence monotone of measurement in terms of off-diagonal elements of positive-operator-valued measure components. This quantification provides a lower bound on the robustness of measurement-coherence that has an operational meaning as the maximal advantage over all incoherent measurements in state discrimination tasks. Finally, we propose an experimental scheme to assess our quantification of measurement-coherence and demonstrate it by performing an experiment using a single qubit on IBM Q processor.</jats:p>
title: Quantifying coherence of quantum measurements

items.abstract:
<jats:p>The coherence of a quantum state with respect to a fixed incoherent basis is typically quantified using distance-based measures. Among these, a particularly intuitive and computationally convenient coherence quantifier is derived from the Hilbert-Schmidt distance. In this work, lever-aging the channel-state duality established by the Jamiolkowski-Choi isomorphism, we introduce a coherence measure for quantum channels based on the Hilbert-Schmidt distance between the
<br>
Jamiolkowski-Choi state and its dephased counterpart, which exhibits a simple mathematical structure and possesses several desirable properties. We further elucidate its information-theoretic significance by demonstrating that it is equivalent to the uncertainty, as quantified by the variance of the Jamiolkowski-Choi state in the incoherent basis. Additionally, we establish a connection between this coherence measure of a channel and the increase of the Tsallis 2-entropy of the corresponding
<br>
Jamiolkowski-Choi state. One more alternative quantifier of coherence for channels is quantified by the generalized Wigner-Yanase-Dyson skew information. We analyze its fundamental properties, including unitary covariance, convexity, and monotonicity under specific operations. To illustrate and compare these two quantifiers, we evaluate them for several prototypical quantum channels, thereby uncovering key information-theoretic aspects of the structure of channels from the perspective of coherence.</jats:p>
title: Quantifying Coherence of Quantum Channels

items.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>Quantum coherence is one of the old but always important concepts in quantum mechanics, and now it has been regarded as a necessary resource for quantum information processing and quantum metrology. However, the question of how to quantify the quantum coherence has just been paid the attention recently (see, e.g., Baumgratz <jats:italic>et al</jats:italic>. PRL, 113. 140401 (2014)). In this paper we verify that the well-known quantum Fisher information (QFI) can be utilized to quantify the quantum coherence, as it satisfies the monotonicity under the typical incoherent operations and the convexity under the mixing of the quantum states. Differing from most of the pure axiomatic methods, quantifying quantum coherence by QFI could be experimentally testable, as the bound of the QFI is practically measurable. The validity of our proposal is specifically demonstrated with the typical phase-damping and depolarizing evolution processes of a generic single-qubit state, and also by comparing it with the other quantifying methods proposed previously.</jats:p>
title: Quantifying quantum coherence with quantum Fisher information
